title: fix(plugin-charts)!: ObjectChartBlock declares its pre-gate props instead of `(props: any)`
body:
Fixes #8885
Clause-②: yes — a published component signature narrows from `any` (ruling 5810232641).

Part 2 of objectui#8885. Part 1 landed as PR #8895. `ObjectChartBlock`, the registry shell that wraps `ObjectChart` behind `ElementDataSourceGate`, now declares its props. Before, it was published as `(props: any)`.

Notation: GitHub strips angle-bracket fragments from PR bodies, so generics are spelled in words below. `Omit OF ObjectChartProps MINUS 'schema'` means the TypeScript `Omit` of `ObjectChartProps` with its `'schema'` key removed.

## What changed

- **`ObjectChartBlock`'s parameter** is now `Omit OF ObjectChartProps MINUS 'schema'`, intersected with `{ schema: BaseSchema }`. Both parts are existing exported names, and no new type is minted.
  - `schema` is `BaseSchema`, the node `SchemaRenderer` hands every registered renderer (the object arm of `SchemaRendererProps.schema`).
  - Every other prop (`dataSource`, `onSegmentClick`) is `ObjectChart`'s own, so the type is **closed**.
- **The one loose member is the hand-off** `schema={bound as ObjectChartSchema}` into `ObjectChart`. That line is where the pre-gate node becomes the component's post-gate schema. The gate maps the `dataSource` binding but does not validate, so the post-gate claim is made there, at one line, and not on the published signature.
  - Measured: this is the single diagnostic the narrowing costs, TS2741 `Property 'chartType' is missing in type 'BaseSchema' but required in type 'ObjectChartSchema'`.
- **Both registrations still type-check.** The shell is registered as `object-chart` and under the `chart` alias. `ObjectChartSchema`'s `type: 'object-chart'` literal would be false for the alias. `BaseSchema`'s `type: string` is correct for both.
- A new compile-time pin, `packages/plugin-charts/src/__tests__/ObjectChartBlock.props-8885.test.tsx`. It is compiled by `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, and `--listFiles` confirms it is in that program.
- A changeset: `'@object-ui/plugin-charts': minor`, with a BREAKING section written in migration terms. Published 17.6.0 ships `ObjectChartBlock: (props: any) => React.JSX.Element`.

### Why `BaseSchema` (the seat's reading)

The ruling types the shell's `schema` as "the registry renderer's raw node input", and it stops only "if no shared pre-gate node type exists to name". `BaseSchema` is exported, and it is exactly what `SchemaRenderer` passes every registered renderer as `schema`, so naming it invents nothing. The dispatch order had added a stricter stop, "if the shells disagree", and the first round of this claim stopped on it. The measured reading was 15 of 17 `elementDataSourceBlock` shells declaring `any`, 1 declaring a component-specific shape and 1 declaring a post-gate schema. That stricter condition was the dispatching seat's, not the ruling's, and the seat lifted it, choosing option A of the `needs_decision` report on the card.

## Evidence (final HEAD `5fb961c13`)

**Consumer cost, measured before writing** with the objectui#7483 comment 5647422745 method. Only plugin-charts' `dist` was re-emitted, and each type-check leg ran separately. Re-run at `5fb961c13` against the head `dist`:

| leg | exit | `error TS` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| plugin-charts `tsc --noEmit` / `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| plugin-dashboard src / test | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| runner src / test | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| app-shell src / test | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| console src | 0 | 0 |
| example-console-starter src / test | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| example-schema-catalog src / test | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| example-byo-backend-console src | 0 | 0 |
| site src (after `next typegen`) | 0 | 0 |

No dependant references `ObjectChartBlock` by name. Both registrations go through `ComponentRegistry`, which is `Registry OF any`, and `registerLazy` loaders are typed `() => Promise OF unknown`. The built `dist/index.js` is byte-identical to the base build (`cmp` exit 0). The only `dist` change is `ObjectChart.d.ts`: the `ObjectChartBlock` declaration and its docblock, plus the `BaseSchema` type import.

**Red on base, green on head.** For the red leg, the pin file stayed at HEAD while `ObjectChart.tsx` was set back to its base blob (`6ad6d4e1` to `1f26145d`, proven by hash). Then `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` exited 2 with 8 errors:
- TS2344 on `assertionShellParamIsNotAny`, `assertionShellSchemaIsNotAny`, `assertionSchemaIsTheRawNode` and `assertionRestIsObjectChartProps`;
- TS2578 (unused `@ts-expect-error`) on P1 (misspelled prop name `dataSorce`), P2 (`schem`), P3 (string `schema`) and P4 (node without `type`).

Controls C1 (the `chart` alias node), C2 (a binding-only node `{ type, dataSource: { object, view } }`) and C3 (`ObjectChart`'s own props passed through) compiled on both sides. It was restored with `git checkout HEAD --` and proven by blob `6ad6d4e1` == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`. On head, `pnpm run type-check` for plugin-charts runs `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` and exits 0.

**Closedness ablation.** Adding `[key: string]: any` to the props type through `ablation-replace.mjs` reds exactly `assertionRestIsObjectChartProps` (TS2344) and P1 (TS2578). The any-guards and P2 to P4 stay green, so P1 catches an open props bag, not only `any`. Output: `ok mutation landed: anchor 1 -> 0` and `ok restored: blob == HEAD (6ad6d4e17f77)`.

**Tests.** `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/plugin-charts/` plus three `packages/types` census tests that read `ObjectChart.tsx` as text (`object-chart-undeclared-keys-8885`, `widget-schema-anchors-7946`, `base-bind-declared`) gave `Test Files 77 passed (77)` and `Tests 874 passed (874)`. That is 74 plugin-charts test files plus the 3 census files, so every file ran.

**Lint.** eslint on the 2 touched source files, with `--no-inline-config --format json`, reported 0 errors. `ObjectChart.tsx` has 41 warnings against 42 on base: one fewer `no-explicit-any`, because the `(props: any)` is gone. The pin file has 1 warning, the deliberate `any` in `assertionAnyProbeCanFire`, which proves the any-probe can fire. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` belongs to CI.

**Gates (unlocked, exit captured before any pipe):**
- `check-changeset-presence` exit 0: "3 file(s) changed, 2 of them published source of a package the release covers".
- `check-changeset-no-major` exit 0. `check-changeset-fixed` exit 0. `check:changeset-claims` exit 0 (report-only). `check:pending-changeset-literals` exit 0.
- `check:new-line-citations` exit 0: "VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)".
- `check:control-bytes` exit 0.
- `check:element-data-source-declaration` exit 0: "all reach the seam and take it from core".
- `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check-type-check-coverage`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:doc-fences` and `check:shell-escape-residue`: each exit 0.
- `check-governed-queue-guard --test` on the 3 paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- `check:readme-exports` exit 1 is PREREQUISITE NOT MET: 417 self-imports unjudgeable because their packages' `dist` is not built. None is in plugin-charts, and no README or doc mentions `ObjectChartBlock`, so this diff does not reach it. NOT MEASURED, not red.

## Acceptance notes

Noted, not filed:
- **Most other shells still publish `any`.** Read at base `3261e6479`: 15 of the 17 `elementDataSourceBlock` shells publish `schema: any`, and two of them (object-map and object-timeline) publish a bare `React.FC OF any`. This PR types only `ObjectChartBlock`. A family-wide pre-gate type was option C of the decision, and it was not taken. Carrier: none.
- **The two published examples of this pattern disagree.** The `@object-ui/react` README types the shell `FC OF { schema: BaseSchema }`, as this PR now does. The `elementDataSourceBlock` doc comment beside `ElementDataSourceGate` shows `elementDataSourceBlock OF React.FC OF any`. Carrier: the next edit to that file.
- **Ceiling.** A misspelled key INSIDE the node (for example `objectNme`) still compiles, through `BaseSchema`'s passthrough index signature. That is protocol-level, not this card's; the pin keeps a counter-probe so the ceiling stays visible.
